question: In humans, which parent determines the sex of the child?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Father**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• In humans, the determination of the sex of a child is a **genetic process** governed by the **23rd pair** of chromosomes, known as the **sex chromosomes**.

• Human beings have a total of **46 chromosomes** or **23 pairs**. Out of these, **22 pairs** are **autosomes** (identical in both males and females), and the **last pair** defines the biological sex.

• The female genetic makeup consists of two **X chromosomes** (**XX**). Consequently, all **gametes** (eggs) produced by a mother contain only an **X chromosome**.

• The male genetic makeup consists of one **X chromosome** and one **Y chromosome** (**XY**). This means the **father** is **heterogametic**, producing two types of **sperm**: one carrying the **X chromosome** and the other carrying the **Y chromosome**.

• The sex of the child depends entirely on which type of sperm fertilizes the egg. If a sperm with an **X chromosome** fuses with the egg, the resulting child will be **XX (female)**. If a sperm with a **Y chromosome** fuses with the egg, the child will be **XY (male)**. ***Hence, the father is the parent who determines the sex of the child.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Chromosomal Basis of Sex**:

• The mechanism where specific chromosomes determine the sex of an individual is called **sex determination**. In humans, this is the **XY system**.

• During **meiosis**, the chromosome pairs separate so that each **gamete** receives only one chromosome from each pair.

• Since the **ovum** (egg) always contributes an **X**, the **zygote's** sex is determined at the moment of **fertilization** by the **male gamete**.

• **Probability of Sex**:

• Statistically, there is a **50% chance** of having a boy and a **50% chance** of having a girl in every pregnancy, as the ratio of **X-carrying sperm** to **Y-carrying sperm** is **1:1**.

• **Other Systems in Nature**:

• Not all organisms follow the **XY system**. For instance, in **birds**, the system is **ZW**, where the **female** (ZW) is the **heterogametic** sex and determines the sex of the offspring, while the **male** is **ZZ**.

• In some **reptiles**, sex is determined by **environmental factors** like the **incubation temperature** of the eggs rather than genetics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **The SRY Gene**:

• The **Y chromosome** contains a specific gene called the **SRY gene** (**Sex-determining Region Y**).

• This gene is responsible for the initiation of **male sex determination** by triggering the development of undifferentiated gonads into **testes**.

• In the absence of a **Y chromosome** (and thus the **SRY gene**), the biological default pathway leads to the development of **ovaries** and a female phenotype.

• **Historical Context**:

• The chromosomal theory of sex determination was discovered in the early **20th century** (around **1905**) by American geneticists **Nettie Stevens** and **Edmund Beecher Wilson**.

• Their work shifted the understanding of heredity from vague external factors to specific **microscopic structures** within the **cell nucleus**.

• **Misconceptions**:

• In many cultures historically, mothers were wrongly blamed for not bearing a male child. Scientific evidence clearly shows that the **mother's genetic contribution** to sex is **constant (X)**, and the **father's contribution** is the **variable factor**.
